mainTopic: Why the תורה wrote out each of the אבות נזיקין separately even though a מה הצד could teach most of them: each category has its own special law.
overview: The גמרא keeps asking why the תורה wrote out every main category of damage. It suggests writing only two categories and learning the rest from them, but it rejects this, because one category cannot be learned from two. רבא disagrees: if בור is one of the two sources, every category can be learned through a מה הצד except קרן, because all the others are מועד from the start. According to the view that קרן is actually the more serious case, since it means to cause damage, even קרן can be learned. So the גמרא asks why the תורה wrote them all out, and answers that each category has its own special law. קרן teaches the split between תמה and מועדת, שן and רגל are exempt in רשות הרבים, בור is exempt for vessels (or for a person according to רבי יהודה), and אדם pays four extra payments. אש is exempt for טמון. The amud ends by asking what אש teaches according to רבי יהודה, who makes one pay for טמון, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Suggestion: write only two categories and learn the rest
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תורה could have written just two of the main damage categories and learned the others from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה write only two categories, and we would learn the other ones from those two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still asking why the תורה needed to write out every category of damage. It now suggests a shortcut: write only two and learn the rest from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the גמרא showed that one category alone cannot teach another, because each one has its own special features. Now it tries a stronger tool: combine two sources. What two sources share in common might be enough to teach a third case.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the תורה or ה׳
Two
And let it come, meaning let it be learned
The other one(s)

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write two,
phrases.notes: Two of the main damage categories, like שור, בור, מבעה and הבער.

phrases.english: and let the other be derived from them;

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא תַּרְתֵּי, וְתֵיתֵי אִידַּךְ מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion that one category cannot be learned from a single other category, now trying two.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the תורה to write every category of damage separately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If two written categories could teach the rest, writing all of them seems extra.

steps.title: Rejected: one category cannot be learned from two
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is turned down: even two categories together cannot teach another one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he said: one category cannot be learned from two.
steps.whatsHappening: The same speaker answers his own suggestion. Even two categories together are not enough to teach a third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each category has its own special features. Whatever two sources share, there is still something about them that the third case does not have. That difference blocks the derivation, so writing all the categories is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Then he said, often meaning he took back or answered his own suggestion
One from two
Cannot be derived

phrases.aramaic: הֲדַר אָמַר: חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי לָא אָתֵי.
phrases.english: Then he said: one cannot be derived from two.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר: חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי לָא אָתֵי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two written categories could teach all the others.
steps.terutzMaskana: No combination of two categories can teach a third, so each must be written.

steps.title: רבא: With בור as a source, all can be learned except קרן
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if בור is one of the sources, every category can be learned through a מה הצד, except קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: For all of them, when you put בור together with them, all of them can be learned through a מה הצד, except קרן. That is because there is a way to refute it: what is special about all the others is that they are dangerous from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the idea that one cannot be learned from two. He says that if בור is one of the two sources, every category can be learned, with one exception: קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מה הצד takes what two sources have in common and applies it to a third case. רבא says that pairing בור with any other category teaches the rest. קרן is left out because all the other categories are מועד from the start, meaning their damage is expected, while an ox that gores is a תם for its first three gorings.

keyTerms.meaning: You throw in or add
A pit, one of the main damage categories
Through the common factor that two sources share
To refute, to break a derivation
Considered dangerous from the very start

steps.confusionAlert: רבא does not say קרן is not one of the main damage categories. He only says the מה הצד cannot teach it, because the others are מועד from the start and קרן is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the final question of the section: if almost everything can be learned, why did the תורה write each category out?

phrases.english: Rava said:
And all of them, when you cast Pit among them,
all of them can be derived through the common factor,
except for Goring;
because there is room to refute:
what about all of them? They are forewarned from their outset.
phrases.notes: An ox that gores starts out as a תם, so it is not like the others.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וְכוּלְּהוּ כִּי שָׁדֵית בּוֹר בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the claim of step 2: with בור as one source, a מה הצד does work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With בור as one of the sources, every category can be learned through a מה הצד except קרן, because all the others are מועד from the start.

steps.title: According to the other view, even קרן can be learned
steps.stepSummary: According to the opinion that קרן is actually more serious, because it intends to damage, even קרן can be learned through the מה הצד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says, 'On the contrary, קרן is more serious because it intends to cause damage,' even קרן can be learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings in a different opinion that sees קרן as the more serious case. According to that view, רבא's one exception disappears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's refutation only works if being מועד from the start makes the others more serious than קרן. The other view says קרן is worse, because the ox means to cause harm. If so, the refutation fails and קרן is learned along with everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Horn, meaning goring, one of the main damage categories
Is stronger or more serious
Its intention is to cause damage

phrases.english: And according to the one who says: On the contrary, Goring is superior,
as its intent is to damage;
even Goring can also be derived.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's statement: under the other view, even the one exception falls away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the view that קרן is more serious, קרן too can be learned through the מה הצד.

steps.title: Then why did the תורה write them all?
steps.stepSummary: If every category can be learned, why did the תורה write each one out?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, for what law did the תורה write them all?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that every category can be learned, the גמרא asks why the תורה bothered to write each one out. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 3 and 4 seem to make writing the categories unnecessary. The תורה never writes extra words, so there must be a reason each one appears.

keyTerms.meaning: But then
For what law
Wrote them

phrases.english: But for what halakha did the Merciful One write them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a problem from steps 3 and 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fact that the תורה wrote each category out separately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a מה הצד can teach every category, writing them all looks extra.

steps.title: Answer: for their own special laws
steps.stepSummary: The תורה wrote each category to teach the special laws that belong only to that category.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: each category is written to teach the laws that are special to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic duty to pay could be learned through a מה הצד. But each category also has its own unique details, and those can only come from its own verse. So writing each one is not extra.

keyTerms.meaning: For their own laws, the details unique to each category

steps.whatToRemember: Even if the basic liability for most categories could be learned through a מה הצד with בור, the תורה wrote each category to teach its own special laws.

phrases.english: For their own halakhot.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives each verse its own purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The categories are written for no reason, since they could be learned.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each category is written to teach its own special laws.

steps.title: The special law of goring: first-time goring versus a known gorer
steps.stepSummary: קרן was written to teach the difference between a תמה and a מועדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Goring was written in the תורה to show the difference between an animal that has not yet become known as a gorer and one that is known to gore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins listing the special law that each category teaches. The first is קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מה הצד could tell us that goring makes the owner pay. It could never tell us that an animal not yet known to gore (תמה) pays only half damages while a known gorer (מועדת) pays full damages. That split exists only in קרן, so the תורה had to write קרן out.

keyTerms.meaning: Goring; damage an animal does on purpose, such as goring
An animal that has not yet built up a pattern of goring; its owner pays half damages
An animal that is known to gore, with a warned pattern; its owner pays full damages
To make a distinction between

phrases.english: Goring (was written)
to distinguish between an innocent animal and a forewarned one.
phrases.notes: An innocent animal's owner pays half damages. A forewarned animal's owner pays full damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first example of the general answer given in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Unique-law explanation: the explicit verse is needed for a rule no derivation could produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If every category can be learned through a מה הצד, writing קרן seems unneeded.
steps.terutzMaskana: קרן is written to teach the split between תמה and מועדת.

steps.title: The special law of eating and trampling: no liability in the public domain
steps.stepSummary: שן and רגל were written to teach that the owner is exempt when the damage happens in רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Eating and trampling were written to teach that the owner does not pay when they cause damage in a public area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second special law, which belongs to שן and רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals naturally eat and walk as they move through public streets. The תורה wrote שן and רגל out to teach that damage of this kind in a public area is exempt. A מה הצד would only have taught that the owner is liable, so it could not teach this exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Tooth; damage an animal does by eating for its own benefit
Foot; damage an animal does just by walking
The public domain, an area everyone uses
To exempt them from paying

phrases.english: Eating and trampling (were written)
to exempt them in the public domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of special laws.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Writing שן and רגל seems unneeded if they could be derived.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are written to teach the exemption in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: The special law of the pit: no liability for vessels
steps.stepSummary: בור was written to teach that the owner of a pit is exempt when vessels fall in and break.
steps.simpleTranslation: The pit was written to teach that the pit's owner does not pay for objects that fall into it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the special law of בור according to the regular opinion. The pit owner does not pay for damaged vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit owner pays when an animal falls in. Damaged objects, however, are exempt, and only the explicit writing of בור teaches that. A מה הצד could not create an exemption like this.

keyTerms.meaning: Pit; an obstacle someone leaves where it can cause damage
Vessels, objects, belongings
To exempt from paying

phrases.english: Pit (was written)
to exempt vessels with regard to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of special laws.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is written to exempt vessels.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה: the pit is exempt for a person
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that a pit owner does pay for vessels, so for him the special law of בור is that it is exempt when a person falls in and dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says the pit owner does pay for broken vessels. So for him, the pit was written to teach that the owner is not liable when a person dies from falling in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the special law of בור, because רבי יהודה disagrees about vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer from step 9 does not work for רבי יהודה, since he makes the owner pay for vessels. The גמרא finds a different exemption that he still agrees to: the death of a person. Either way, בור has its own special law.

keyTerms.meaning: Who holds liable
Damage to vessels

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two opinions. The regular view exempts vessels. רבי יהודה makes the owner pay for vessels and exempts a person instead.

phrases.english: And according to רבי יהודה,
who holds one liable for damage to vessels in a pit,
(it was written) to exempt a person with regard to it.
phrases.notes: The case is a person who falls into the pit and dies.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דִּמְחַיֵּיב עַל נִזְקֵי כֵלִים בְּבוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a replacement answer for בור that fits רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי יהודה the vessels exemption does not apply, so בור seems to have no special law.
steps.terutzMaskana: For him, בור teaches the exemption for a person.

steps.title: The special law of a person: four extra payments
steps.stepSummary: אדם was written to make a person who injures someone pay four extra kinds of payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person was written to make him pay for four extra things when he injures someone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list with the special law of אדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's owner pays only for the damage itself. A person who injures another person also owes four more payments. No other category has this, so the תורה had to write it out.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who causes damage
To make him liable
Four extra payments, beyond paying for the damage itself

steps.whatToRemember: Every category of damage has its own special law that no derivation could teach. קרן has the split between תמה and מועדת. שן and רגל are exempt in רשות הרבים. בור is exempt for vessels, or for a person according to רבי יהודה. אדם pays four extra payments. אש is exempt for טמון, as step 12 explains, and step 13 asks what אש teaches according to רבי יהודה. This is why the תורה wrote each one out.

phrases.english: Man (was written)
to make him liable for four things.
phrases.notes: These four come on top of paying for the damage itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of special laws answering the question in step 5. אש follows in step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is written to add four extra payments.

steps.title: Fire was written to exempt hidden items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that אש has its own special law: the person who started the fire is exempt for items that were hidden and got burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fire was written to exempt the owner from paying for hidden items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list and gives the special law of אש: hidden items (טמון) that burn do not have to be paid for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like קרן, שן, רגל, בור, and אדם before it, אש needed to be written because it has a unique rule. If someone's fire spreads and burns things that were hidden, such as under a pile of grain, he does not pay for them. Learning אש from the other categories would never have taught this exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: Fire, one of the main categories of damage
To exempt from paying
A hidden or covered item, for example one buried under grain

phrases.english: Fire was written to exempt, through it, a hidden item.
phrases.notes: "Hidden item" means something covered up, like a vessel buried in a pile of grain, that the fire burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of unique laws for each אב נזיקין, now turning to אש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a unique law that justifies writing the category separately
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think אש adds nothing new and could be learned from the other categories.
steps.terutzMaskana: אש teaches a unique exemption: hidden items that burn are not paid for.

steps.title: What does fire teach according to רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last answer using רבי יהודה, who holds that one does pay for hidden items burned by fire. For him, what special law does אש teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי יהודה, who makes a person pay for hidden items damaged by fire, what does fire come to add?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer just given only works for the רבנן. It asks what new law אש teaches according to רבי יהודה, and the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a person does pay for hidden items burned by his fire. So for him the טמון exemption does not exist, and the reason given in step 12 for why אש was written falls away. This is the same pattern as step 10, where רבי יהודה's view about vessels in a בור needed a different special law.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds that one must pay
Damages of
To add what? What new law does it come to teach?

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not saying אש is not a category of damage. He only disagrees about the טמון exemption, so the גמרא needs a different special law to explain why אש was written.

phrases.english: And according to רבי יהודה, who holds one liable
for damage to hidden items by fire,
what does it come to add?
phrases.notes: He means: what special law makes it necessary for the תורה to write אש separately?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה דִּמְחַיֵּיב עַל נִזְקֵי טָמוּן בָּאֵשׁ, לְאֵתוֹיֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 12's answer by pointing out that רבי יהודה disagrees with the טמון exemption.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that אש was written to exempt טמון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה holds a person does pay for טמון burned by fire, so for him that exemption cannot be the reason אש was written. Some other special law is needed.
